Children, adults and AI agents explore a game world the same way at first; an exoskeleton for 50 kg loads; the robotics radar.
TECH RADAR
Children, adults and AI agents follow the same curiosity when exploring
No. 16 · Friday 6 November 2026 · Robotics and automation · 6 min read
 
IN 30 SECONDS
1A Berkeley study in PNAS finds that children, adults and AI agents first seek novelty and then seek control when exploring an open game world, and that children who talk to themselves about goals may explore better.
2At Scuola Superiore Sant'Anna in Pisa, a 32 kg exoskeleton helps workers walk, squat and step over obstacles while carrying loads of up to 50 kg.
3Robotics radar: research grows faster this year than in the previous three, led by robots that learn, and new humanoid-robot projects on GitHub nearly tripled in a year.

new robotics papers today
+30%
robotics research momentum this year compared with all research
+182%
new GitHub projects on humanoid robots, Q3 2026 vs Q3 2025
SIGNAL OF THE DAY
What drives exploration: children, adults and AI agents compared
Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences · 4 November · Free PDF  Journal  High-impact journal
Who wrote it: Aly Lidayan and 5 others · University of California, Berkeley (United States) · among the authors Pieter Abbeel, h-index 137
Context. Robots that learn by trial and error need a reason to try new things when nobody tells them what to do, an artificial 'curiosity'. Researchers have proposed several mathematical versions of curiosity, but it is unclear which ones resemble how people actually explore.
The team watched adults, children aged 8 to 12 and AI agents explore Crafter, a simple open-world game, and compared their behaviour with three measures of curiosity: seeking variety, seeking new information, and seeking situations where you have more control. All three go with progress in humans, and variety and control matter more for children. Both humans and agents first chase variety, which then levels off, while the drive for control keeps growing: early on they look for new places, later for situations they can master. There are also early signs that children who talk to themselves about their goals explore better. It is today's signal because it gives robot learning a human benchmark for curiosity, and the data are public for others to build on.
PAPERS OF THE DAY · ROBOTICS AND AUTOMATION
Robot manipulation and learningstrong growth
Research share +59% in 3 years · 3,074 papers in 2025
What it is about. Lab robots already mix and measure liquids following set recipes. The hard part is the long list of small hands-on jobs, setting up, adjusting, cleaning, that still need a person.
TARMAC as a taxonomy for robot manipulation in chemistry
Communications Chemistry · 4 November  Journal  High-impact journal  Free PDF ↗
Who wrote it: Keting Huang and 8 others · among the authors Ian J. S. Fairlamb (University of York), h-index 56
WHAT THEY DOBy studying how chemistry procedures are taught, they build a catalogue of 18 basic hand actions, sorted by how much force they need, how direct they are and whether they repeat, and test some on real robots.
RESULT904 of 917 manual steps in 23 lab procedures fit the 18 actions; robots performed 8 of them in five tasks on four different robot setups.
WHY IT MATTERSA shared 'vocabulary' of lab movements makes it easier to compare robots and automate the messy parts of lab work.
Prosthetics and rehabilitation roboticsstable
Research share −2% in 3 years · 2,609 papers in 2025
What it is about. Exoskeletons for workers aim to make heavy lifting and carrying less tiring and less harmful. Most load-carrying models only help on flat walking.
WeLEx: Design, control, and performance of a novel portable lower-body occupational exoskeleton for power assist in load carrying
Robotics and Autonomous Systems · 1 November  Journal  High-impact journal  Free PDF ↗
Who wrote it: Alberto Nobili and 6 others · Scuola Superiore Sant'Anna (Italy) · among the authors Antonio Frisoli, h-index 47
WHAT THEY DOA 32 kg motorised exoskeleton for the hips and legs, with cables that share the effort between hip and knee so less weight sits at the feet. One control system handles several activities and loads.
RESULTIn tests of walking, squatting and stepping over obstacles, it assisted the wearer while carrying loads of up to 50 kg.
WHY IT MATTERSHelping with more than flat walking is what logistics and construction work need; tests were functional demonstrations, not a workplace trial.
Autonomous vehicles and safetygrowing
Research share +45% in 3 years · 3,340 papers in 2025
What it is about. Turning right at a city junction, a car crosses the path of pedestrians and cyclists. A self-driving car must guess a few seconds ahead where everyone is going.
A Risk-Aware Lightweight Vehicle Trajectory Prediction Framework for Right-Turn–VRU Interactions at Urban Intersections
Systems · 1 November  Journal  High-impact journal  Free PDF ↗
Who wrote it: De Zhao, Shengpeng You, Runze Mou · Southeast University (China)
WHAT THEY DOA compact AI model that predicts a turning car's path while paying most attention to the pedestrians and cyclists who pose a real risk, rather than to everyone nearby.
RESULTIts average position error is 0.68 metres, 16% lower than the model it builds on, and 28% lower in the riskiest right-turn conflicts; a much larger model is more accurate still.
WHY IT MATTERSSmall, accurate models can run on the car itself, where the risk to pedestrians and cyclists is highest.
RADAR OF THE DAY · ROBOTICS AND AUTOMATION
What it is about. Machines that sense their surroundings and act in the physical world: factory arms, warehouse robots, self-driving vehicles, medical robots. Robots increasingly learn from examples and experience instead of being programmed step by step.
+23%

+30%
momentum this year compared with all research
19.5%

Where research is growing (topic share, 2022→2025)
Robot manipulation and learning
grasping and handling objects; this year it almost doubles its pace
▲ +59%
Power line inspection robots
machines that check cables and pylons instead of technicians
▲ +56%
Reinforcement learning in robotics
robots that improve by trial and error, as in today's signal; also nearly doubling its pace
▲ +46%
Autonomous vehicles and safety
vehicles that drive themselves, and how to make them safe
▲ +45%
Robot path planning
choosing routes that avoid obstacles and people
▲ +41%
What developers and the public do
SIGNALGITHUB
(year on year)		HACKER NEWS
(year on year)
«humanoid robot»▲ +182%▲ +115%
«robot learning»▲ +147%▼ −20%
GitHub: new projects; Hacker News: stories discussed (only 8 for robot learning). Q3 2026 vs Q3 2025; for comparison, all new GitHub projects grew 62% and Hacker News discussions fell 38%. Wikipedia, 12 months: views down for humanoid robots (−15%), self-driving cars (−39%) and industrial robots (−21%). Data updated 3 November.
In short: Research and developers move together on robots that learn and on humanoids, which are also the only robotics topic discussed more than a year ago; general public curiosity, measured on Wikipedia, keeps falling.
WORDS OF THE DAY
h-index — a measure of how often a researcher is cited: an h-index of 50 means 50 papers cited at least 50 times each. Above 40 usually indicates an established name in the field.
Intrinsic motivation — doing something because it is interesting in itself, not for a reward, like a child exploring a new playground.
Reinforcement learning — a way for robots and AI to learn by trial and error, keeping what works, much like learning to ride a bike.
Exoskeleton — a wearable frame that supports or strengthens the body, for example to carry heavy loads with less effort.
WORTH WATCHING
Tomorrow the weekend overview compares the five verticals. Worth watching: whether robot-learning methods start to borrow from how children explore, as today's signal suggests.
